body.question: Which sections do my notes now fall into?

{"id":29,"answer":"Your saved notes don't carry explicit section labels, so this is an inferred grouping based on note content and timestamps rather than a declared structure. As best I can tell from the notes provided, they fall into roughly these buckets:

• Java / DSA study notes — type erasure (List<String> erases to List, no instanceof List<String>, no new T[]), ArrayList vs LinkedList access and insert/remove costs, checked vs unchecked exceptions and try-with-resources ordering.
• Notes-app product feedback — wanting to see which notes were used versus just cited ids, and the cited-vs-related distinction being too subtle.
• Bugs / system behaviour — queued structure reviews being coalesced so one supersedes the other, flagged as by design.
• Architecture & decisions — retrieval being lexical plus graph with embeddings deferred to v2; the site later becoming an extension with default context tracking to organize info.
• Meetings — the Arjun meeting where retrieval approach was decided and he took ownership of structure review.
• Tasks / reminders — the DBMS assignment PDF due Friday 11:59pm on the portal with the ER diagram.
• Finance — 5000/month SIP into the index fund on the 3rd, 6-month emergency fund target.
• Drafts / writing — the LinkedIn post draft about a local-first notes app, needing a first-line hook and maybe a privacy angle.
• Technical implementation notes — SQLite FTS5, bm25() being lower-is-better and requiring ORDER BY rank, and external content tables needing sync triggers.
• Unclassified / test data — the note containing null byte, bell, and line separator characters, which reads like an encoding/storage test rather than real content.

Two caveats: the "sections" here are my groupings, not names your notes themselves use, and the counts are small enough that some of these would probably merge (for example, product feedback, bugs, and architecture all belong to the same DeepNotes project thread, while the Java notes and the DBMS/reminder notes are the study cluster).","references":{"coverage":"partial","general_knowledge":false,"explanation":"The notes contain no explicit section or category metadata, so the sections had to be inferred from note content, which is why coverage is partial rather than sufficient.
